Quanta third-party notices

Quanta's own source is licensed under the accompanying MIT LICENSE.
Third-party components retain their own licenses; the app's MIT license does
not replace those terms. Exact upstream notices are in licenses/ in the
portable package and docs/licenses/ in the source archive. These notices
are also embedded in the standalone executable.

DEPENDENCIES.json records exact installed package versions, notice paths and
SHA-256 hashes. It includes runtime packages and build utilities, and is an
inventory, not a certification that every package is used at runtime.
Python's LICENSE includes notices for bundled components; Pillow's LICENSE
includes its bundled image/codec libraries. Tk's notice is included separately.

pystray is LGPL-licensed. Its LGPL/GPL notices and unmodified installed Python
source accompany this distribution. The complete Quanta source and pinned
Windows build dependency list allow rebuilding the application with a modified
pystray. Quanta imposes no additional restriction on modification or reverse
engineering needed to debug modifications to that library.

proxy_tools 0.1.0's installed metadata says MIT, but its source header and
upstream LICENSE.txt use BSD terms. We include the actual upstream notice:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jtushman/proxy_tools/master/LICENSE.txt

Windows, Microsoft .NET and Microsoft Edge WebView2 are operating-system/runtime
dependencies and retain their respective terms. No offline WebView2 installer
is included. Quanta falls back to a text panel if its webview backend cannot start.

To rebuild with a changed library, extract the matching source package, create
a Python 3.12.14 x64 environment, install requirements-windows-build.txt, apply
the library change in that environment, regenerate license inventory, run the
tests, then run build_windows.py. Build locally; do not upload personal .aibar data.
